Pfingsten.et: From Middle High German phingesten, from Late Latin pentēcostē, from Ancient Greek πεντηκοστή (pentēkostḗ). The Old High German form fimfchusti is a partial calque of the Ancient Greek term, with πεντη- (pentē-) replaced by fimf (“five”). Cognate with Hunsrik …

Pfirsich.et: From Middle High German pfërsich, from Old High German phërsih, from Proto-West Germanic *persik (“peach”).

s: trifle (anything of little importance or worth)
Weiter nichts? versetzte der Fuchs. Das ficht mich nun alles / Keinen Pfifferling an.[…]
Pfifferling.et: Middle High German phefferlinc, Old High German phiferia, related to Pfeffer (“pepper”). In the figurative sense apparently a reference to its (former) ubiquity.
